subject: Aligning stakeholders for 75-minute ML infra lab — calendar options & agenda
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Sam Torres <sam.torres@atlashealth.ai>, Priya Menon <p.menon@atlashealth.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 20 Aug 2025 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Aligning stakeholders for 75-minute ML infra lab — calendar options & agenda

Hi Sam / Priya —

Great to meet earlier today. Quick recap: Atlas Health is trying to validate a low-latency serving path for clinical summarization, and you want a short, production-focused lab so your infra and ML teams can sign off on latency, cost, and integration approach.

Proposed next step: a 60–90 minute technical deep dive (we typically do 75 minutes) with our ML infra engineers + your ML/infra leads. Goals for the session:
- Walk a short sample prompt/throughput run with a representative model.
- Validate latency targets and batching behavior with your expected qps.
- Surface integration options (hosted vs dedicated vs VPC private) and required network/KMS constraints.
- Confirm mutual action plan and success criteria for a pilot.

Please find two scheduling options below — pick any that work for your team, or suggest alternatives:
1) Thurs Aug 28, 10:00–11:15 PT (preferred by our ML lead)
2) Tues Sep 2, 13:00–14:15 PT

Attendee ask from your side: could you confirm 2–3 people who will join and their roles (ML lead, infra/cloud engineer, security/compliance contact if possible)? On our side Ben (runtime lead) and Grace (solutions/ops) will join.

I attached a short scope doc and a draft agenda (tdx-readout-agenda-v1.docx) — rough items and timeboxing. If you have a simple dataset we should load (de-identified), please share a short sample or a pointer to S3.

If helpful I can also send a brief pre-call checklist (ports, VPC peering options, KMS info).

Thanks,

Mina Haddad
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192
Redwood Inference

Attachments: atlas_prelim_scope.pdf (pdf), tdx-readout-agenda-v1.docx (docx)
From: Sam Torres <sam.torres@atlashealth.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 21 Aug 2025 09:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aligning stakeholders for 75-minute ML infra lab — calendar options & agenda

Thanks Mina — good summary and appreciated the clear goals. Priya and I reviewed the two slots and the team prefers Thu Aug 28 10:00–11:15 PT.

Attendees from Atlas:
- Sam Torres (ML lead)
- Priya Menon (Infra lead)
- Daniel Liu (SRE) — will join if the slot is final

We have one ask up front: can Ben plan to run a short throughput demo with 100 concurrent simulated requests to show tail latency behavior? That’s the core concern for the product team. Also, Priya asked for a short note on network requirements — whether we need VPC peering or if a simple egress/IP allowlist is enough for the demo.

I can confirm the sample dataset (de-identified) by EOD Aug 25 and share an S3 link.

Sam

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 21 Aug 2025 11:16:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aligning stakeholders for 75-minute ML infra lab — calendar options & agenda

Thanks Sam — good call locking the 28th. Quick notes from my side so the Atlas team knows what to expect:

1) Throughput demo: I’ll run a short load profile that includes a 60s warmup and then a 30s steady-state at ~100 concurrent requests (we’ll simulate with realistic seq lengths you mentioned). We’ll capture p50/p95/p99 and tail latency distributions and share results in the call.

2) Infra checklist: for the demo we can operate over TLS with an allowlist of Redwood egress IPs; VPC peering isn’t required for the initial lab unless you need to test private-only access. If you want us to test with customer-managed KMS, please share KMS key ARN and a test role we can assume (we’ll provide a minimal IAM policy).

3) Prep ask: if you can upload a 200–500 record anonymized sample to S3 by EOD Aug 25 and send the link, Grace and I will pre-load it into our run harness. Alternatively, we can use a synthetic sample but real samples make the run much more informative.

4) Timeboxing: planned agenda (75m): 5m intro, 20m sample run + live metrics, 15m architecture/integration discussion, 20m tradeoffs (batching/quant/throughput), 10m next steps and pilot scope.

See you Thu — Ben

Ben Carter
Senior Runtime Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

All set for Thu Aug 28 10:00–11:15 PT — calendar invite accepted (we added Daniel as tentative). Thank you for the checklist Ben. A couple quick clarifications from infra:

- We will provide an S3 link with a pre-signed URL by Aug 25 EOD.
- For the allowlist approach, please share the egress IPs and port ranges you need.
- If Redwood needs to assume an IAM role to pull data, we’ll create a test role with s3:GetObject and log it in the agenda doc.

One more ask from security: can we get a short note on data retention for the demo run (how long artifacts/metrics/logs are kept)? Not needed before the call but good to have in the mutual action plan.

Thanks — Priya

Priya Menon
Infra Lead, Atlas Health
priya.menon@atlashealth.ai
